tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent (app slowness, alarm questions, IOPS sizing, modification stuck, snapshot review, KMS errors, bill jumps, pre-launch review) rather than internals, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including implicit phrasing ('even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower'), and explicitly excludes out-of-scope domains. It is a dense but reasonably concise paragraph given the breadth of the skill's scope.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user wants to know why Amazon EBS storage is slow, why an EBS alarm fired, or whether their EBS setup is production-ready, even if they only say an app or database on EC2 got slower or ask whether to add IOPS.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts (e.g., what EBS or CloudWatch is) and instead jumps directly into domain-specific classification tables, workflow steps, and gotchas specific to EBS. It is dense but all content is non-obvious domain knowledge.
tests.evidence: Load only the reference files the request needs.' and the classification table mapping user phrasing to specific paths — all project/domain-specific, no generic explanations.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large reference tables (API docs, error codes, thresholds) are embedded in the body; details are consistently deferred to references/ files, including inside the classification table which links out rather than inlining content.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ (data-collection, ebs-best-practices, finding-logic, metrics-thresholds, review-operational, review-report-format, troubleshoot-billing, troubleshoot-encryption, troubleshoot-performance, troubleshoot-snapshots, troubleshoot-volume-modification) has at least one markdown link in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Links are embedded in a classification table and workflow steps that specify the triggering condition (e.g., user phrasing, metric alarm) for when to load each file, and the References section footnotes describe content briefly but conditions are established earlier in the body.
tests.evidence: | "My app is slow", high latency, an alarm on AWS/EBS metrics... | Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md](references/troubleshoot-performance.md) |

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/filename.md with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (modification limits, deletion refusal, approval flow) are given exact prescriptive rules, while flexible analytical tasks (classification, drafting the report) explain purpose and let the agent reason through classification table and verdict format rather than micromanaging every sub-step.
tests.evidence: Use current service rules: up to 4 Elastic Volumes modifications per volume per rolling 24 hours.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same task as equal options; it designates specific APIs/paths per scenario via the classification table rather than listing alternatives.
tests.evidence: The classification table maps each trigger to exactly one path/reference, with no competing tool menu presented.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable classification + workflow approach (classify request, load references, run path, validate) that applies across many EBS troubleshooting/review scenarios rather than declaring a single specific task outcome.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Classify the request / Step 2: Load the shared references / Step 3: Run the path and draft the report / Step 4: Check the draft, fix it, then present it

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill includes a dedicated Gotchas section with concrete, non-obvious corrections specific to EBS metrics and modification behavior.
tests.evidence: A modification in `optimizing` is not stuck. The new size, IOPS or throughput already applies while it optimizes.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly defines output templates for both troubleshoot verdicts and review reports, satisfying the need for structured output guidance.
tests.evidence:
